subject: Healthline private offer — approval path and term recommendation
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Mike King <mike.king@healthline.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Healthline private offer — approval path and term recommendation

Hi Mike,

Great to connect last week — thanks for the time. As promised I wanted to follow up with a concrete private-offer proposal and a suggested approval path so you can see how this would flow through Healthline (and what we need from procurement/finance to move to PO).

Key callouts: 
- Offer: Redwood private offer via AWS Marketplace (seller-guided).
- Pricing: $0.045 per token-equivalent compute unit (blended), with an alternate vCPU-based option we can price at ~$1.20/vCPU/hr for steady-state inference (happy to show math).
- Term options: 12 months (standard) or 24 months (discounted ~12% MSRP).
- Activation: once PO is received we can activate within 48 hours; DocuSign signature optional if you prefer contract first.

From experience with similar customers, the common approval lane is: Procurement -> Legal redline check (usually limited for AWS private offers) -> CFO/Finance sign-off when deal > $200k ARR. For a 12-month pilot-sized commitment we typically see procurement + head of platform approve without CFO.

I've attached a short proposal and an evidence pack for your security team. Can you confirm which approvers we should include on the PO and whether Healthline requires a multi-BU PO vs single legal entity? That will determine whether we route as a single private offer or split across buyer accounts.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm approver roster (procurement + finance contacts) and preferred term (12 vs 24).
2) We issue an official private offer and DocuSign (if needed) + activation checklist.
3) You route PO into procurement queue — we aim for activation within 48 hours of receipt.

If helpful I can host a 20-min walk-through with Vivek (engineering lead for field success) to answer any technical activation questions for the marketplace listing.

Thanks,

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- proposal-healthline-PO.pdf (pdf)
- healthline-evidence-pack.zip (zip)

From: Mike King <mike.king@healthline.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@healthline.com>
Date: 2028-04-22 14:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Healthline private offer — approval path and term recommendation

Hi Naomi,

Thanks — this is helpful. A few quick answers:
- Preferred term: We want to start with 12 months for the pilot, but we are open to 24 months if the discount is material after the pilot.
- Approvers: Please include Procurement (procurement@healthline.com) and our Finance lead (tara.singh@healthline.com). If the value comes in under $150k we can likely avoid CFO sign-off. Over that, CFO will need to be looped.
- BU split: We'll run the pilot under one BU/legal entity to simplify procurement. If we expand, we will add additional buyer accounts.

Can you confirm the activation SLA and whether we can get the private offer keyed to our marketplace account ID (acct-hl-9943)? Also, procurement needs the invoice cadence (annual vs monthly).

Thanks,
Mike
Mike King
Director of Engineering, Healthline
mike.king@healthline.com | 206-555-8877

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@healthline.com>, Mike King <mike.king@healthline.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-23 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Healthline private offer — approval path and term recommendation

Thanks Mike — noted on approvers and single BU. Quick answers to your questions below and next steps.

Activation SLA: 48 hours after we receive the signed PO (or DocuSign completion) and confirm the buyer marketplace account ID. We will provision the private offer tied to acct-hl-9943.

Invoice cadence: Default is annual in advance for private-offer commitments; we can support quarterly invoicing by request (procurement preference).

Attached is a version of the private-offer proposal with explicit pricing lines (12-month and 24-month). If procurement wants the PO language we can provide a standard AWS private-offer activation template that lists the SKU, term, and billing cadence.

To speed approvals, suggested minimal fields you can include in the PO: buyer legal entity, AWS marketplace account ID (acct-hl-9943), Purchase Order number, term start date, and invoice cadence. No countersignature from Redwood is required for the private offer itself; DocuSign is optional and handled as a commercial agreement if you need it.

I recommend we do the following this week:
- Procurement: confirm invoice cadence and PO number format (if available).
- Healthline: confirm whether your legal requires a commercial MSA — if yes, legal will want to review; if no, private-offer + PO is enough.

I'll leave Vivek and Karthik on the thread to confirm technical items and to prepare the offer for AWS.

Best,
Naomi

Attachments:
- proposal-healthline-PO.pdf (revised)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-24 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Healthline private-offer approvals / invoice cadence

Internal notes (do not forward without checking signatures):

Team — a few internal items to confirm before we issue the private offer to AWS: 
1) Pricing model preference: Mike asked about token-equivalent vs vCPU/hr. For pilot simplicity let's offer the blended token-equivalent line (simpler to communicate expected spend). If they choose 24 months we can present the vCPU/hr option as a secondary SKU.
2) Invoice cadence: offering quarterly invoicing reduces procurement friction — approve leaving flexibility in the proposal to switch to annual on final PO.
3) Approval thresholds: finance told me yesterday that deals under $150k we can self-approve; above that we need revenue ops + finance sightline. Our deal estimate (12m pilot) = ~$120k, so should stay under the CFO threshold.
4) Evidence pack: confirm we include SOC 2 summary and sample audit logs. Karthik, can you confirm the evidence pack link is the most recent?

Karthik: please attach the healthline-evidence-pack.zip I prepared and confirm the SKU IDs we will send to AWS. I will draft the private-offer creation checklist for Naomi to send to Healthline.

Vivek
VP, Field Success | Redwood Inference

Naomi: once you confirm procurement's cadence preference and PO number we will create the offer and send the activation link + DocuSign option.
